identity_evidence.quote: A 68-year-old female of Asian ethnicity presented with a 1-year history of heartburn and significant weight loss.

attribution_limitations: Table 1 places discharge at T = +14 days relative to admission with laparotomy at T = +3 days, whereas the text gives discharge on postoperative day 14, which would be 17 days after admission. This is an arithmetic-level mismatch recorded as an ambiguity, not a source conflict.

The incision exudate and incision imaging are dated "the second postoperative day". The only operation described is the laparoscopy converted to laparotomy (T = +3 days), so a literal reading would place them before the first discharge, but the sentence follows the readmission and perforation narrative and describes stool from the incision connected with the cystic lumen; Table 1 instead places fistulography confirmation at T = +15 days. The source does not state which reference point is meant.

The tuberculosis diagnosis rests on necrotic granulomas considered tuberculosis plus positive tuberculin skin and interferon-gamma release assay results; microbiological confirmation was not performed, and the discussion calls it the most likely underlying etiology while elsewhere calling it active abdominal TB.
The CT finding is called peritoneal effusion in the text and ascites in the abstract and Table 1.

The table places initiation of antituberculosis therapy at T = +15 days, while the text says it was given after consultation at the tuberculosis hospital without a time, and says the condition stabilized after more than 1 month of treatment while the table says T = +2 months. The text says the abdominal drainage was withdrawn after 1.5 years (home care after discharge) while the table gives T = +1.5 years relative to admission.

The authors say the case highlights considering tuberculosis in the absence of definitive ovarian tumor tissue, while the pathology reports a benign ovarian mucinous cystic adenoma; ovarian malignancy is never stated as excluded.
The postoperative fever of up to 39 ℃ and its improvement are stated without a time; the sudden fever of 39 ℃ occurred that evening after discharge.

Figure 5 prints the label "Sinus tract leading to the skin" on the right-sided arrow, while the caption calls the right-sided finding an established enterocutaneous fistula; no time is stated for this CT.
